title: One dataset, two doctrines
content: Post-treatment Borrelia DNA/antigen and animal persisters are accepted by both camps; they diverge only on interpretation. Lyme arthritis is uniquely informative because DMARD/synovectomy response is a falsifying test the rest of chronic-Lyme lacks.

title: Autoantigen panel as a refractory-arthritis biomarker
content: ECGF, Annexin A2, MMP-10, apoB-100 reactivity could prospectively identify antibiotic-refractory patients who should go straight to DMARDs.

title: Cellulose vs. keratin: the irreducible core fact
content: The entire dispute reduces to whether filaments are textile cellulose (CDC/Hylwa) or endogenous keratin/collagen (Middelveen) — resolvable by blinded spectroscopy that conspicuously has not been done jointly.

title: Real symptom, disputed cause
content: Formication and lesions are agreed real; the fight is purely causal. 'Real vs fake' misdescribes Morgellons; the honest framing is organic dermatosis vs delusional infestation vs a heterogeneous mix.

title: One symptom, two communities, zero shared attribution
content: Identical formication is read as a reversible drug effect in stimulant forums and as chronic infection in Lyme/Morgellons forums, with almost no cross-reference — a natural experiment in attribution.

title: Abstinence challenge as a clean partition
content: Stimulant-caused formication should resolve with sustained abstinence; an abstinence-challenge protocol could prospectively separate stimulant-driven from non-drug Morgellons.

title: Mechanism mainstream, only the pathogen in question
content: Infection->autoimmune basal ganglia->OCD is accepted for streptococcus (PANDAS). The Lyme-OCD claim needs only to show Borrelia uses the existing mechanism — a concrete, testable target.

title: Arthritis supplies the human autoimmunity proof
content: Lyme arthritis proves Borrelia induces organ-specific autoimmunity in humans (ECGF, Annexin A2) — the strongest indirect support for taking Lyme-OCD seriously, rarely cited in that debate.

title: Treatment-resistant Lyme is often untreated babesiosis
content: A meaningful fraction of 'Lyme that won't improve on doxycycline' is co-existing babesiosis that doxycycline does not treat — a point where mainstream and patients agree and acting helps real patients.

title: Validated parasite next to fringe parasite claims
content: A strong mainstream parasite (Babesia, validated assays) sits beside fringe claims (novel protozoa, rope worms, non-validated commercial tests). Assay validity cleanly sorts the two.

title: Two additive suicide-risk routes converge
content: A biological route (neuroinflammation/quinolinic acid) and a psychosocial route (chronic pain + medical invalidation) both operate; co-infection severity amplifies both. The psychosocial route is the most modifiable.

title: Invalidation as a modifiable suicide-prevention target
content: Clinician validation of real suffering amid diagnostic uncertainty could be studied as a suicide-prevention measure independent of the etiology debate.

title: The syphilis analogy smuggles in the disputed conclusion
content: Spirochetal homology is real, but syphilis's late persistence is demonstrable while treated-Lyme CNS persistence is the contested claim. The analogy is a strong hypothesis-generator that imports the very thing in dispute.

title: Immunosuppression exposes Lyme's serology dependence
content: HIV-Lyme cases show Lyme diagnosis breaks down when the antibody response is altered — fragile exactly in patients where infection may matter most.

title: Minority intuition directionally right, specifically wrong
content: Borrelia genuinely suppresses humoral immunity (vindicating 'Lyme wrecks the immune system'), yet the specific CD57 biomarker built on that intuition remains unvalidated.

title: Immune disruption is the project's mechanistic spine
content: Humoral suppression explains imperfect serology, reinfection, co-infection synergy, atypical HIV presentation, and neuroinflammatory tone — connecting most other topics.

title: Two true facts fused into one false one
content: True: US researched weaponizing ticks and Burgdorfer participated. True: Lyme surged late-20th-century. False weld: therefore Lyme is the escaped weapon — broken by ancient-DNA evidence the narrative omits.

title: Ancient DNA is the decisive, under-deployed counter
content: Otzi's Borrelia and 15-My amber spirochetes refute an engineered organism while leaving legitimate historical disclosure questions (2019 DoD-IG review) intact.

title: Persistence vs. post-infectious is the master variable
content: Topics 1,4,5,6,7,8 all hinge on whether the pathogen persists alive or triggered a self-sustaining process and left. The honest synthesis is both/and: residual antigen + induced autoimmunity + real-but-likely-non-causal persisters.

title: 'Validated diagnostic?' sorts credible from fringe
content: The portable quality filter across the database: validated assays (Babesia smear/PCR, two-tier serology, CD4) are mainstream; unvalidated ones (CD57, novel-parasite commercial tests, endogenous-filament claims) are fringe-leaning.

title: The controversy is a terminology collision
content: Late disseminated Lyme, PTLDS, and 'chronic Lyme disease' get fused into one word; most arguments are really about which one is meant. Both camps largely agree post-Lyme illness is real and that prolonged antibiotics lack controlled support.

title: Right about the illness, contested on the mechanism
content: PTLDS's recognition plus objective findings (small-fiber neuropathy, interferon-alpha) vindicate that the illness is real and biological, but do not vindicate the persistent-active-infection mechanism or prolonged antibiotics.

title: The congenital-syphilis analogy cuts both ways
content: A related spirochete (Treponema) transmits transplacentally and sexually, making the vertical/sexual questions for Borrelia legitimate. But syphilis does so via sustained spirochetemia and mucosal shedding that tick-adapted, briefly-bacteremic Borrelia lacks. The analogy both motivates and limits the hypothesis.

title: 'Insufficient evidence' is not 'proven false'
content: Congenital Lyme was removed from ICD-11 for insufficient evidence, not disproof. The spirochete can cross the placenta (rare, esp. untreated), yet a defined congenital syndrome isn't established. The honest frame is 'possible, rare, under-studied, reduced by treating the mother.'
